title: Rear Parking Aid — Audible System Locations
introduction:
I read this rear parking aid map in layers: the sensors across the rear bumper, the controller shown toward the front of the cabin, and the rear audio speakers. Follow each leader line from the transparent vehicle to its enlarged component, then use the table to identify it. The enlarged pictures show what the parts look like; their position around the page is not their position in the car.

PAM means parking assist control module, and this reference identifies it as integral to the BCM. That distinction matters when identifying the controller: the map does not present PAM as a separate box to go hunting for.

Choose the speaker entries for the vehicle’s body style. The table distinguishes convertible speakers from those labeled sedan, and LH and RH mean left-hand and right-hand. Those rear speakers are part of the audio system. The bumper sensors and cabin speakers therefore occupy different ends of the audible parking-aid story: the ears and the voice, so to speak.

This is a location guide for vehicles equipped with rear parking aid. It does not give trim-removal steps, wiring connections or an operational test. Use it to establish which component and body-style entry you are looking at before moving to the matching service or diagnostic information.

edits.text: Audible Rear Parking Aid Component Locations
edits.why: The drawing connects the rear bumper sensors, integrated controller and body-style-specific audio speakers. Selecting the correct speaker entries prevents the combined illustration from being mistaken for a single vehicle’s equipment layout.
